title: 1981 AHSME Problem 18
statement: The number of real solutions to the equation \[ \frac{x}{100}=\sin x \] is

solutions.text:
The equation is odd-symmetric and has the solution \(x=0.\) On \((0,\pi)\) there is one further positive solution. For each \(k=1,2,\ldots,15,\) the positive sine hump on \((2k\pi,(2k+1)\pi)\) rises above \(\frac{x}{100}\) and then falls below it, giving two solutions. There are no positive solutions beyond \(31\pi\), because the next positive hump begins above \(100\) while \(|\sin x|\le1.\) Thus there are \(1+2(15)=31\) positive solutions, the same number negative, and zero itself: \(31+31+1=63.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is C.
hints: Use odd symmetry and first count the positive solutions
